caption: Jesus is called Messiah—God’s anointed ruler—and Psalm 2 became central to Christian claims about him. But “anointed” was a title shared by many people.

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Did “anointed” identify Jesus? Psalm 2 calls its king God’s anointed. The New Testament calls Jesus Messiah—or Christ, which means anointed.
slides.body: Psalm 2 calls its king God’s anointed. The New Testament calls Jesus Messiah—or Christ, which means anointed.
slides.heading: Did “anointed” identify Jesus?

slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Ps 2:2: against the LORD and against His Anointed One
slides.body: against the LORD and against His Anointed One
slides.heading: Ps 2:2

slides.alt_text: The claimed New Testament fulfilment in Jn 1:41, BSB: He first found his brother Simon and told him, “We have found the Messiah” (which is translated as Christ).
slides.body: He first found his brother Simon and told him, “We have found the Messiah” (which is translated as Christ).
slides.heading: Claimed fulfilment · Jn 1:41

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: The royal connection is important Early Christians deliberately presented Jesus as God’s promised Davidic ruler and used Psalm 2 about him.
slides.body: Early Christians deliberately presented Jesus as God’s promised Davidic ruler and used Psalm 2 about him.
slides.heading: The royal connection is important

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: But many people were anointed Kings, priests and others carried this title. The word alone cannot identify Jesus.
slides.body: Kings, priests and others carried this title. The word alone cannot identify Jesus.
slides.heading: But many people were anointed

title: The title Christ
